Specialty Bolt & Screw, Inc. · SBS Product Training Item: /OETIK16704021-1500Oetiker 16704021 Stepless Ear Clamp, 36.5 mm, Stainless Steel

Topic T1 · First Impression

What You'd Notice Picking This Up Cold

Item F1 is a single-ear clamp: a stainless steel band formed into a ring, with one raised loop — the ear. Slip it over a hose, close the ear with a pincer tool, and the ring shrinks down onto the hose and fitting.

Item F1 on a millimeter grid: a closed stainless ring with a single raised “ear”.
The item’s 3D model from the SBS website — the ring, the ear and the row of locking windows.
Where You'd Find It
The VMI bin card this module is named after — Item F1 lives in cell F1 (boxed in orange): “EAR CLAMP STAINLESS STEEL 36.5MM”.
The physical bin: column F, row 1 — the front row of the tray. The orange box marks where Item F1 sits.
Parts of the Clamp
Click the photo to enlarge.
The parts of the clamp, numbered.
  1. The ear — the raised loop. Pinching it closed with a tool takes up band length and clamps the ring down. Its inside width is 10 mm.
  2. The band — 18-8 stainless strip, 7 mm wide and 0.6 mm thick.
  3. Locking windows — the punched openings where the band’s overlapping end locks once the clamp is closed. The print’s side view draws them too.
  4. Overlapping inner end — the band end tucks inside the ring. The print calls this a Stepless Ear Clamp.
  5. The ear, edge-on — seen from the side, the ear stands up from the band; this is where the closing tool grips.
At a Glance

Name

Stepless Ear Clamp — the title on the Oetiker drawing. The SBS category calls it an Ear Clamp.

Single Ear

The item specification lists the pinch clamp style as Single — one ear per clamp.

Material

Stainless steel, 18-8 (A2), with a plain finish.

The part number /OETIK16704021-1500 doesn’t spell out the size or material — it points back to the supplier and the supplier’s part number. See .

Reading a Part Number Like an Engineer

Not every SBS part number spells out its specifications. /OETIK16704021-1500 has a clear structure — a leading slash, a supplier prefix, the supplier’s own part number and a dash suffix. This module follows the part from the website to the print to the inspection bench.

Topic T2 · Part Number Decoder

Four Parts of a Part Number

Hover over any element of the part number below to see what it means — the same way SBS reads a new item, one piece at a time.

/OETIK16704021-1500  =  OETIKER # 16704021 36.5-706R
Reading the Prefix
The same item on its product page: Item #, the Customer Part # (BRP part # 509000529, active) and the description.

Reading the Prefix

  1. The slash. Marks a catalog or print part.
  2. OETIK. The supplier prefix — the first five letters of the supplier’s name, Oetiker.
  3. 16704021. Oetiker’s own part number — the same number in the title block of the Oetiker drawing.
  4. -1500. A dash suffix on the SBS item number. It is not part of Oetiker’s part number.
Reading the Item Description

OETIKER #

The supplier name, Oetiker, followed by its part number.

16704021

Oetiker’s part number. It matches Part No. 16704021 on the drawing.

36.5

The clamp’s nominal diameter in millimeters — the Maximum Clamp ID of 36.5 mm on the item specification, and the “36.5” marked on the clamp itself.

706R

The rest of Oetiker’s size code. The 7 and 06 line up with the 7 mm band width and 0.6 mm band thickness on the drawing.

Topic T5 · The Oetiker Print

Reading the Oetiker Drawing

/OETIK16704021-1500 is a catalog part, so its print is Oetiker’s own customer drawing for part 16704021, the Stepless Ear Clamp. Most of the drawing is notes — written in German, English, French and Spanish.

The Oetiker Drawing
Click the drawing to enlarge.
Oetiker drawing 151.006.002, revision a — Part No. 16704021, Stepless Ear Clamp.
  1. Theoretical diameter range: 33.3 – 36.5 — the website’s min and max clamp ID.
  2. Weight: 5.1 g — one clamp.
  3. Assembly — this clamp must only be assembled with tools recommended by Oetiker.
  4. Diameter check — the diameter has to be checked on a plug gauge.Plug gauge: a precision pin of a set size, used to check an inside diameter.
  5. Inscription — the * on the drawing marks where the clamp is stamped with its nominal diameter and the company logo.
  6. Material — X5CrNi18-10 (1.4301) and UNS S30400: the European and American names for 304 stainless.
  7. General tolerances — DIN ISO 2768-mK, for any dimension without its own tolerance. All dimensions are in millimeters.
  8. Part No. 16704021 — the number in our part number, with the description Stepless Ear Clamp.

Topic T6 · Inspection

How the Part Is Checked Against Print

When a lot is inspected, the clamp is checked against the Oetiker drawing and the results are recorded on the SBS Inspection Report.

The Inspection Report
Click the report to enlarge.
The Inspection Report for /OETIK16704021-1500: PPAP level 4, BRP # 509 000 529, with the Oetiker drawing attached as the print page.
  1. Burrs / Thread Aesthetic — visual, pass / fail.
  2. Material / Finish — 304 SS, checked visually and against documents.
  3. Dim 1 = Clamp Range — 36.00 – 37.00 mm, caliper.
  4. Dim 2 = Band Thickness — 0.50 – 0.70 mm, caliper.
  5. Dim 3 = Ear Inside Width — 9.30 – 10.50 mm, caliper.
  6. Dim 4 = Band Width — 6.90 – 7.40 mm, caliper.
  7. Marking — OET/36.5, visual, pass / fail.
Report vs. Drawing

Inspection Report

The SBS report carries the PPAP level (4), part number, BRP number and the print page, then one row per feature with its reference or min and max, its method, and sample columns (up to 18 samples) for a Pass / Fail result. The ballooned sketch numbers Dims 1–4 on the clamp.

Oetiker Drawing

The dimensions come straight from drawing 16704021: nominal plus or minus its tolerance gives the report’s min and max.

Visual & Document Checks

Burrs, material (304 SS) and the OET/36.5 marking are checked visually or against documents.

Caliper Checks

Clamp range 36.00–37.00; band thickness 0.50–0.70; ear inside width 9.30–10.50; band width 6.90–7.40 mm.

Topic T7 · Materials, Grades & Finishes

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

The website calls it 18-8 (A2) stainless steel, the drawing calls it X5CrNi18-10, and the inspection report calls it 304 SS. They are all the same steel.

Material

Stainless Steel.

Grade

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel.

Finish

Plain — no plating or coating.

On the Report

Material / Finish: 304 SS.

Three Names, One Steel

18-8 (A2)

18-8 is an American term for stainless steel with about 18% chromium and 8% nickel. A2 is the ISO name for the same 304 family.

X5CrNi18-10

The European steel name on the drawing: X = high-alloy steel, 5 = 0.05% carbon, CrNi 18-10 = about 18% chromium and 10% nickel.

1.4301 & UNS S30400

1.4301 is the European material number; UNS S30400 is the American number for type 304. Both appear in the drawing’s material block.

Why Stainless for an Ear Clamp
  • Corrosion resistant — good in the fluid and air systems ear clamps are used on.
  • Formable — the band can be formed into the ear and pinched closed without cracking.
  • Plain finish — stainless needs no plating to resist rust.
SBS Material Cross-Reference
SBS’s own materials cross-reference — the same 304 stainless under every country’s standard, including DIN 1.4301 and UNS S30400 from the Oetiker drawing. Try the Material Conversion tool ↗

Topic T8 · Applications

Where Ear Clamps Are Used

Ear clamps secure hoses onto fittings. Closing the ear with a tool compresses the band evenly around the hose, giving a uniform, tamper-resistant seal.

Fluid Systems

Holding hoses on fittings where leak prevention matters.

Air Systems

Securing air lines to their fittings.

Vibration Resistance

Consistent clamping force that holds up on equipment that moves and shakes.

Compact Installation

A low-profile band with no screw housing — useful where space is tight.

Installing an Ear Clamp
  • Slide it on — place the open clamp over the hose and fitting.
  • Close the ear — pinch it with a tool recommended by Oetiker, as the drawing requires.
  • Tamper-resistant — once closed, the clamp is not meant to be loosened and reused.
Single Ear vs. Two Ears

Same Idea, Different Style

The Ear Clamps category page shows a two-ear clamp. Item F1 has a single ear — the item specification lists its pinch clamp style as Single.

The two-ear style from the category page, for comparison.

Reference

Glossary

Every code, acronym, and term used in this module, defined in plain language. Tap a term’s “jump” button to see it in context.

18-8 (A2) Stainless Steel

Stainless steel with about 18% chromium and 8% nickel; A2 is its ISO name. Equivalent to type 304, the grade of this clamp.

Catalog or Print Part

The leading “/” in the part number marks a catalog or print part — one specified by a supplier part number or a print.

Customer Part # (BRP)

The customer’s own number for an SBS item. This clamp is BRP PART # 509000529 (ACTIVE).

DIN ISO 2768-mK

The general tolerance standard on the Oetiker drawing. It sets the tolerance for any dimension that doesn’t carry its own.

Ear

The raised loop on an ear clamp. Pinching it closed with a tool takes up band length and clamps the ring down.

Ear Clamp

A band clamp that secures a hose onto a fitting when its ear is compressed with a tool, creating a uniform, tamper-resistant seal.

Oetiker

The supplier behind this part. “OETIK” in the part number is the first five letters of its name, and 16704021 is its part number.

Plug Gauge

A precision pin of a set size, used to check an inside diameter. The Oetiker drawing says the clamp diameter is checked on one.

PPAP

Production Part Approval Process — the documentation package that proves a supplier can reliably make a part to print. This item is at PPAP Level 4.

Stepless

From the drawing title, Stepless Ear Clamp: the band’s end tucks inside the ring rather than leaving a step.

VMI

Vendor Managed Inventory — SBS stocks bins at the customer. The sample box and its bin card follow the same layout; this item is cell F1.

X5CrNi18-10 / 1.4301 / UNS S30400

European steel name, European material number and American UNS number for 304 stainless — all in the drawing’s material block.
